correctness.rationale: For each nonzero cyclic difference d the Sidon property isolates a unique product; inverse DFT of each intensity gives exactly the cyclic correlation. Its two-mask ratio is the root of unity \(\omega^{(r_1-r_0)d(a+b)}\); prime-field inverses reconstruct both ordered endpoints. All off-diagonal pair products follow. For three or more atoms the identity \(P_{ji}P_{ik}/P_{jk}=|x_i|^2\) provides all diagonal entries, and the Gram matrix reconstructs x up to common phase. For two atoms the quadratic \(q^2-Eq+|P|^2\) has precisely one or two distinct positive assignments; one atom has p possible locations. One-mask shift and any-number-of-phase-masks swap are exact. Gaussian-integer checker confirmed 4983 finite cases; the proof covers all odd primes and arbitrary complex coefficients.

originality.rationale: Comparisons by mathematical implication identify no same-object prior two-prescribed-unimodular-quadratic-mask reconstruction for every prime-cyclic Sidon support with exact fibers and sharp mask count. The primary 2026 paper treats unmasked ambiguities; the 2013 sparse theorem has generic/modulo-shift scope; the 2015 two-mask theorem uses zero-containing masks and zero padding; the chirp Gabor record measures an \(N^2\) Gabor orbit. An unindexed older deterministic masked diffraction result remains possible.

value.rationale: A deterministic two-measurement-setting threshold and complete fiber classification answer a natural phase-mask design question on the noncollision sparse class. Algebraic endpoint decoding removes the usual translation/reflection ambiguity, while the unavoidable one- and two-atom failures identify fundamental phase-only information limits. These are natural classes and full regimes, not a parameter slice or minor improvement; no computational downstream application beyond reconstruction is claimed.
